title: APDEX-Driven Eval Prioritization and Annotation Lifecycle Playbook
author: Derek Huang
content:
Overview

Purpose: Provide a concrete operational playbook that uses an APDEX-inspired scoring signal to prioritize evaluation probes, schedule annotation work, and enforce annotation SLAs aligned to product-level SLOs (latency/quality/cost). This doc defines the metric mapping, prioritization buckets, scheduling architecture, annotation lifecycle, monitoring expectations, and a regression-runbook for APDEX degradations.

Scope: Applies to evaluator pipelines, probe generators, annotation vendors/queues, and the eval-scheduler service used by the Eval Harness. This is intended for mixed workloads (shadow, synthetic, production probes) across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Why APDEX for eval ops

- APDEX (Application Performance Index) adapted here gives a single summary score for probe-level utility: combining fidelity, timeliness, and failure rate into a unit we can schedule by.
- Advantages: straightforward thresholds, monotonic prioritization, easy-to-instrument SLAs, and interpretable cost/benefit tradeoffs for annotation spend.

Definitions and signals

- probe_apdex: a normalized score in [0.0, 1.0] representing the evaluator utility of a probe. Higher is better. Computed per-probe and aggregated per-slice.
- fidelity_component: measures semantic alignment with golden answers (0–1). Methods: BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, embedding similarity thresholding for open outputs, and human QA pass rate when available.
- timeliness_component: age and expected relevance score (0–1). Newer user-origin probes get higher score; stale model-output or synthetic probes get lower.
- reliability_component: success rate of deterministic replay + tokenization/format normalization pass (0–1).

probe_apdex = 0.5 * fidelity_component + 0.3 * timeliness_component + 0.2 * reliability_component

(APDEX weights above are default; teams may adjust per workload with approval from Evaluation Infrastructure)

APDEX thresholds and scheduling policy

- Priority buckets (APDEX ranges):
  - P0 (critical): 0.0–0.25 — immediate human review, auto-escalate to regression triage.
  - P1 (high): 0.25–0.5 — fast-path annotation (high-quality crowd or L2 SRE review within 24 hours).
  - P2 (standard): 0.5–0.75 — batched annotation during regular cycles (48–72 hours).
  - P3 (low): 0.75–1.0 — low-cost automated labeling or deferred human review (weekly).

Mapping to evaluator actions:
| APDEX range | Scheduler action | Annotation SLA | Annotation mode | Cost control |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| 0.0–0.25 | immediate queueing to "fast-path" | 4 hours | expert annotator + reviewer | emergency budget flag |
| 0.25–0.5 | priority queue | 24 hours | high-quality crowd | flexible burst credits |
| 0.5–0.75 | standard queue | 48–72 hours | pooled crowd | batched economics |
| 0.75–1.0 | deferred/auto | weekly | automated heuristics / synthetic | minimal spend |

Scheduling architecture and implementation notes

- Eval-scheduler service responsibilities:
  1) Ingest probe metadata and computed probe_apdex.
  2) Assign priority bucket and target SLA window.
  3) Create annotation tasks with required label schema and expected TTL.
  4) Respect tenant and model-level quotas and cost budgets.
  5) Emit metrics to telemetry: eval_scheduler.assigned, eval_scheduler.delay_seconds, eval_scheduler.requeue_reason.

- Example scheduler configuration (YAML):

```yaml
scheduler:
  default_weights: { fidelity: 0.5, timeliness: 0.3, reliability: 0.2 }
  buckets:
    - name: critical
      range: [0.0, 0.25]
      sla_hours: 4
      annotator_type: expert
    - name: fast
      range: [0.25, 0.5]
      sla_hours: 24
      annotator_type: high_quality_crowd
    - name: normal
      range: [0.5, 0.75]
      sla_hours: 72
      annotator_type: pooled_crowd
    - name: deferred
      range: [0.75, 1.0]
      sla_hours: 168
      annotator_type: automated
```

- Queueing and batching: For P2/P3 batches the scheduler will group probes by schema (label set) and model variant to maximize annotation reuse and lower cost. Target batch size defaults:
  - P1: 8–16 probes per task
  - P2: 32–128 probes per batch
  - P3: variable, up to 512 when pushing to synthetic heuristics

Annotation lifecycle and contracts

1) Task creation: include probe_apdex, slice tags, golden examples, required annotation schema, and an expiration TTL.
2) Annotation step: annotator completes labels, flags corner-cases, and records confidence score (0–1).
3) Validation: automated validators (format, inter-annotator agreement threshold) run immediately. Tasks below agreement threshold are kicked to L2 review.
4) Ingestion: validated labels are written to the eval-store with provenance tags (annotator_id or system_id) and annotation_latency_ms.
5) Cost accounting: each task records cost_center, annotator_tier, and credits_used. These feed the Eval Budget Ledger.

Inter-annotator agreement (IAA) policy

- Target IAA by bucket:
  - P0/P1: Cohen's Kappa >= 0.7 or majority agreement >= 80%
  - P2: Kappa >= 0.6 or majority >= 70%
  - P3: relaxed; automated heuristics accepted if confidence >= 0.85

Monitoring, SLOs and alerts

- Key metrics to publish (per-slice and per-model):
  - eval.apdex.mean and eval.apdex.p50/p90/p99
  - eval_scheduler.latency_seconds.bucketed
  - annotation.sla.breach_rate (count/% of tasks exceeding SLA)
  - annotation.cost.per_probe_usd
  - iaa.below_threshold_count

- SLOs (example):
  - Annotation SLA adherence: 95% of P1 tasks completed within 24 hours (per-week rolling).
  - APDEX stability: No more than 5% weekly drop in mean probe_apdex for production slices without an associated rollout or config change.
  - Annotation quality: 98% of tasks in P1/P2 pass automated validators on first submission.

- Alerting thresholds (Pager/Slack):
  1) P0 volume spike: pager if >50 P0 probes in 1 hour for a single model.
  2) SLA breach rate: Pager if annotation.sla.breach_rate > 10% for P1 over 6 hours.
  3) APDEX collapse: Pager if eval.apdex.mean drops by >0.2 for a production slice in 30 minutes.

Runbook: when APDEX drops or P0s appear

1) Triage owner: Evaluation Oncall picks up the P0 alert.
2) Rapidly collect context: last deploys, model variant, probe slices, recent tokenization failures, and recent scheduler logs. Use CLI helper: `rds-eval query --slice <id> --last 500 --fields probe_apdex,fidelity_component`
3) Isolate cause: run replay against shadow model (see Shadow Orchestrator playbook). If failing deterministically, mark model as candidate for rollback and open rollback change in Deployment Console.
4) Annotation triage: pause automated ingestion for the affected slice, spawn small expert annotation batch to confirm behavioral regression.
5) Communicate: post incident channel summary and tag owners for product impact.
6) Postmortem: if the drop crosses the regression-impact index threshold, follow Regression Triage handbook for root cause and quality repair.

Rollout and calibration guidance

- Start with conservative weights (fidelity 0.6, timeliness 0.25, reliability 0.15) for any new family of probes for first two weeks.
- Run A/B of scheduling policies for 2-week windows: measure annotation cost per useful-fix and mean time to detect semantic regression.
- Perform quarterly audit of APDEX components per model family to ensure component metrics align with human judgement.

Operational considerations and caveats

- APDEX is an aggregate heuristic; do not use probe_apdex alone to block model promotions. Use it as a prioritization signal combined with targeted shadow evaluations and human checks.
- Weight tuning is workload-sensitive (chat vs. code vs. search). Always record the weight set used in the evaluation-run metadata.

Appendices

A. Example CLI to inspect scheduler backlog:
```
# list top 50 P0 probes for model x
evalctl backlog list --model redwood-open-7b --min-apdex 0.0 --max-apdex 0.25 --limit 50 --fields probe_id,created_at,probe_apdex,slice_tags
```

B. Example probe metadata JSON (stored with probe object):
```
{
  "probe_id": "p-734b9",
  "model": "redwood-open-7b/v1",
  "slice_tags": ["billing-chat", "us-east"],
  "fidelity_component": "0.12",
  "timeliness_component": "0.8",
  "reliability_component": "0.9",
  "probe_apdex": "0.33"
}
```
